A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1834 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE 1840 FEDERAL CENSUS — A HEAD FIVE YEARS AFTER THE SCENE, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1840 federal census of Chicago, read line by line off the left sheets in this repository, carries 1 head of this name — “Jam[e]s [?] Morrison” (33SQ-GYYJ-RY, printed page 212, line 19). This project has ruled the head a CANDIDATE and no more: the name agrees and is unique on both sides, but the reader graded the name on the sheet low, and a low-confidence read caps at a candidate however well the name agrees. A candidate is not an identity — nothing is asserted from it, no household of 1840 is carried back, and the ruling is recorded so that a reader can see it was made rather than missed. Under the rule that decided it (L6a low_confidence_caps_at_candidate), by the crosswalk's own ladder (data/research/census_1840/resident_crosswalk.json). LATER EVIDENCE ONLY. The ratified grading ladder binds: an 1839 or 1840 appearance alone is never an 1835 resident, and 1840 household composition is never back-projected to the 1835-07-01 scene. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and an 1840 head is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “MORRISON J M”, 1836-06-24 to 6/22/1836: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 1 of block 38 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L1BL38CHIOT, as printed); lot 6 of block 57 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L6BL57CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $9820.00 (ls1385, ls1386). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $9820.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: MORRISON J M matches James M Morrison: the forename names James M Morrison of the 5 people of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Morrison, J. M.” (poll_1834_075, line 244). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Morrison' agrees with the entry's forenames; 5 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).
